structure: Order (where facts live, status index, frame, rules spine + engineering rules, core model, clock, epoch ladder, NPC minds, economy, text pipeline, advisors, rivals, presentation, audio, planned-by-milestone, open/dispositions) is a sensible dependency order: rules first, then primitives, then systems, then surface. The Status index (36 rows) is the right navigation device and every row resolves to a heading; the roadmap-id column makes the doc-to-roadmap jump one hop.

Navigation works for 'what does system X say and what is shipped' but is weaker for 'which roadmap id owns this text': ids are scattered inline as (planned: id) 78 times and only the Status index aggregates them. The Roadmap-ordered pointers table (about 120 words) is a partial, second copy of the index and can be deleted.

The Where-facts-live table has only 7 rows, all about meta-facts (versions, verify, layer rules). It does not name owners for the facts this file itself duplicates most: communications-backbone ownership (stated 3x), Detection Tech Level (3x), save policy (4x), talk cost (4x), chunk cap (2x), voice register/tone blips (3x), the #1a1f28/#c4a574 palette (3x), pause bit (3x). Adding 8 owner rows would let the duplicates collapse to pointers.

Misplaced or overloaded sections: (1) 'Frame and pillars (shipped)' holds two planned subsections (Player loop, Seed exemplars) so its shipped mark is only true for Pillars. (2) 'Economy and levers' is an 8-row table of every abstraction (Communications Desk, Orbital Pass, Emergencies, Dual Legacy Ledgers) plus assassination and orbital blackout; assassination/cover persecution belongs with Rivals or its own M6 section, blackout/contingencies with an Orbital section, Dual Legacy Ledgers with Epoch ladder. (3) 'Epoch 2+ travel vignettes' (770 words of full design) sits under 'Planned features by milestone' rather than with the Epoch ladder or a design/ file. (4) 'Local AI eval framework' (502 words) sits inside the Text pipeline section though it scores utility AI and rivals too. (5) Audio sits after Presentation but owns the audibility rule that Text pipeline, Conversation paging and Accessibility all depend on; it is also where Glass River Gorge inheritance is restated. (6) Telemetry policy is inside Engineering rules, which is fine, but Engineering rules (1,435 words) is a doc in itself and is nested under 'Rules spine' via one ## heading, so a reader looking for R1-R8 skims 1.4k words of hx- detail.

Mark hygiene: heading marks and the Status index agree in all 36 rows except the items listed in issues. The 'planned unless tagged (shipped)' rule works but makes 'Cognition phases (shipped)' and 'Pacing config (shipped)' each contain planned bullets, which an agent must catch sentence by sentence.

length_options.option: (a) Move fine-grained distant-M6 design into design/<feature>.md, leaving 60-100 word summary + pointer each: travel vignettes (770 -> 90), assassination vectors + counter-assassination + persecution (363 -> 70), orbital blackout and 5 contingencies + scheduler (507 -> 90, keep forecast), Regard/Romantasy detail (552 -> 120), rival archetypes + ambush (~430 -> 130), epoch ladder skins table + rotation + ceilings + stills (1,200 -> 450, keep 7-rung names and P3 rules). Seed exemplars could join.
length_options.tradeoff: Biggest cut with no concept loss and lowest frequency-of-use text leaves the always-loaded file, so an agent loads about 15% fewer tokens per task. Cost: the 'where do I find X' chain gains one hop, concepts can drift from roadmap.yaml scopes unless each design file is listed in the Status index with its owning ids, and the architecture-relevant parts (hubs, slice shapes, R-rules) must stay in DESIGN_NOTES or agents will design M3 without seeing M6 constraints. Needs a docs-truth check that every design/ file is indexed.

length_options.option: (b) Tighten prose without dropping concepts: delete LaTeX and O(n) asides, cut backticked parentheticals that restate field names, collapse paired 'X (Era 1: ...; evolving per rung as ...)' clauses, drop nested '(planned: id)' marks inside already-planned sections (78 marks; about 40 are redundant), shorten long bullets in Direct floor locomotion, Proximity use, Conversation paging.
length_options.tradeoff: Zero structural change and keeps single-file grep. Cost: effort spread across the whole file (high review burden for the owner), risk of dropping a number or invariant (0.22 m, 0.03 m, 0.4 m, 45 deg) if done carelessly; needs a concept checklist or the no-loss diff method used for config.yaml.

length_options.option: (c) Move Engineering rules (1,435 words: Bridge lock, Determinism, State/saves, Launch validation, Telemetry, Tests) to design/engineering-rules.md, leaving a 120-word summary and the R1-R8 table.
length_options.tradeoff: Clean split (these rules map 1:1 to hx-*/pre-* changes, change rarely, and only M1 agents need them). But M1 is the next thing to build, so the next several apply sessions will open that file constantly, and it is where the fix-first security record lives. Drift risk is low since the owners are roadmap ids. Best done after M1 ships.

length_options.option: (e) Deduplicate in place: remove per-section '> Status:' blockquotes that restate the index (about 14, 560 words), delete the Roadmap-ordered pointers table (120), collapse repeated facts to pointers once Where-facts-live owns them (comms backbone x3, Detection Tech x3, save policy x4, talk cost x4, chunk cap, voice register, palette, pause bit: about 600), trim the Dispositions table to ids and a one-line where (about 150).
length_options.tradeoff: Lowest risk and directly supports the one-owner-per-fact principle; agents see each fact once. Cost: sections read less standalone because cross-references must be followed, and the partial-section status quotes are the only place some 'shipped vs planned' nuance lives, so keep those for Core model, Rules spine, Economy.

No drift risk from the edit, but about 25k tokens loaded per read, 4 of every 5 of which are unshipped M4-M6 detail irrelevant to the current work (M1 hardening). Agents will truncate the read (the Read tool already splits it at 25k tokens), which is the real failure mode: they skim and miss the engineering rules or shipped markers.

length_options.option: Recommended combination: (a) + (e) + a light (b) pass on the three densest sections (locomotion, proximity/menus, paging). Leave (c) until M1 ships.
length_options.tradeoff: Lands about 14.2k words, inside the 14-16k target, without moving anything that M1 work needs. Order matters: do (e) first (it needs no new files), then (a), so the pointers you leave are already deduplicated.

sample_rewrites.after: **AI notes.** Owner stipulation: check whether a JEV- or LAYA-style decision network has a runtime place (not JEPA). Verdict, accepted: no decision model in the simulation path. Zero-shot, such a model scores below the majority baseline, its float output breaks bit-exact replay, and it needs about 520 MB of worker memory. Belief maths are integers and misbelief is designed in. An advisory authoring-time gate tier is allowed but is never the pass/fail authority. Runtime selection of pooled lines is by tag and seed over Observations (also a spec rule in `07-text-port-and-history`). A small fine-tuned classifier with its answer frozen into the save is a parked spike (`classifier-spike`). The maths are in Belief and deliberate misbelief; the Ship Mind forecast is in Economy and levers.

**Adjacent-epoch NPC continuity** (`youth -> prime -> elder -> succeeded_by_heir`). With 15-30 years between operatives, Epoch k NPCs aged `youth` (15-29) or `prime` (30-49) are still alive in Epoch k+1 as `prime` or `elder` (50-75), alongside their children and protégés. They remember your predecessor and the one-rung leap (horse couriers to printing charters; steam and telegraph to radio blocs). Elders pass their seats to `lineageId` heirs, and by Epoch k+2 earlier generations are gone.

Room time and watch time are separate clocks. A room runs `stepKinematics` at 60 Hz with `2-15s` deliberation, dwell and cooldown, which suits watching an NPC think, cross a room at `1.4 m/s` and act. If macro plotlines, couriers, stipends and NPC evolution also ticked every `10s`, an epoch (about 8-14 hours: the `50-100 hour` campaign divided by N epochs) would burn out in 15 minutes.
